item.title: Eight Working, Two Wobbling — Portfolio Snapshot 2026-06-21
item.description: Ten positions are active today, ranked by how much return a holding is estimated to deliver above a minimum threshold, adjusted for how durable that business or fund is judged to be. Eight of the ten have reports that open with "The Bet Still Works." Two — both index funds — carry the more cautious headline "The Bet Is Wobbling." Three further positions are paused and carry no ranking. The full ranked list is in The Lineup, and the two positions worth watching closely are picked out in What Stands Out.

item.title: Three Rules Broken, Six Still Holding — 2026-06-17
item.description: Nine active positions span individual companies, broad equity funds, and a government bond, with conviction weighted most heavily toward a handful of businesses where the underlying conditions remain squarely intact. Six of the nine holdings are working as the standing rules require; three have tripped exit signals. Two further positions are currently paused and excluded from ranking and refresh; their situations are noted separately below. The full read on each holding, in conviction order, is in The Lineup.

item.title: Six Working, Three Not — 2026-06-16
item.description: Nine holdings are active across the portfolio as of 2026-06-16, ranked by their expected return and the quality of the underlying businesses. Six carry an unbroken case for holding; three have had at least one of their written conditions fail. Two further positions are currently paused. The highest conviction sits with Amazon, which ranks first and whose bet remains intact across every measured condition. The most immediate readings worth careful attention are All World, SP500, and TOYOTA, each of which has moved into broken-bet territory. The Lineup below sets out the current state of each holding in order.

item.title: Five Still Working, Two Wobbling, One Broken — 2026-06-11
item.description: Nine active positions, one paused. At the top of the table, conviction is strong: the two leading holdings each sit at or below their buying lines, and the standing read on what holding them from here is worth remains firmly positive. Further down, a handful sit comfortably inside their fair-value ranges, while the tail end carries a fund that has drifted to the trim line and one position whose forward return has turned slightly negative. Two holdings are best described as wobbling — the conditions that justified the original bets have not broken entirely, but the picture has shifted enough to warrant careful reading. One position has broken more clearly. The full detail is in The Lineup.

item.title: 2026-06-10 — Mostly Wobbling, Three Bets Still Working
item.description: Nine active holdings make up the portfolio today, with one further position paused on the sidelines. Conviction sits at the top with Booking — the only name that lands at the top of the list today while its underlying bet still works cleanly. Six of the nine notes carry a "Bet Is Wobbling" headline and three carry a "Bet Still Works" headline. Open The Lineup for each position in order, or skip to What Stands Out for the observations that frame the day.

item.title: Mostly Wobbling, Booking and Amazon Hold Steady — 2026-06-07
item.description: Eight positions sit in the portfolio on 2026-06-07, and the picture is mixed. Conviction is strongest at the top, where Booking holds its place as the steadiest bet on the list and PayPal sits in territory the standing rules treat as cheap. The middle of the lineup is calmer than the headlines suggest: two broad world funds, then Berkshire, then the S&P 500 fund. Of the eight, only Booking and Amazon are still described on disk as bets that are working; the other five read as wobbling, and one — the S&P 500 fund — has had its premium quietly priced away. The full order, with prices and a one-sentence read on each, sits in The Lineup; the sharper observations sit in What Stands Out.

item.title: Mostly Wobbling, Only Booking Holds Steady — 2026-06-06
item.description: Eight holdings sit on the desk this morning, and seven of them carry the same verdict: the bet is wobbling. Only Booking still reads as a bet that works. Conviction sits at the top with PayPal — the standing rules now treat the share price as a buying opportunity, and the forward read on holding it from here is the most positive of the lot. Conviction trails at the bottom with Amazon, where the forward read has turned meaningfully negative. The closest wobble worth a careful read sits in the middle of the lineup at SP500, where the share price has drifted to the trim line. See The Lineup for the full pass.
